policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads simply 'on a sabbath' and relegates the longer reading to a mapped textual_variant note, 'Many ancient authorities insert second-first' — so the text rendered lacks δευτεροπρώτῳ.
The presence or absence of the article before σπορίμων is invisible in 'through the grainfields'; the verse's only note concerns second-first, not this unit.
ASV 'plucked the ears, and did eat' distributes one object across two verbs, which English does freely; it does not isolate whether τοὺς στάχυας stood before or after καὶ ἤσθιον.
ASV 'But certain of the Pharisees said, Why do ye...' carries no indirect object; the added αὐτοῖς of the other reading would give 'said unto them'.

ASV 'which it is not lawful to do on the sabbath day' renders an unmarked infinitive 'to do' and the preposition 'on'; the base ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν needs neither, and 'that which is not lawful on the sabbath' would be idiomatic English without them.
ὁπότε and ὅτε are both simply 'when' in 'when he was hungry'; the only note here is a cross_reference.
'they that were with him' renders οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ with or without the participle ὄντες; the English relative clause supplies the copula either way.
ASV 'how he entered into the house of God' renders ὡς explicitly; the reading that omits it leaves nothing for 'how'.
ASV 'took and ate the showbread' fits either the participle λαβὼν ἔφαγεν or the finite ἔλαβεν καὶ ἔφαγεν; ASV routinely coordinates a circumstantial participle with 'and'.
ASV 'and gave also to them that were with him' has an adverbial 'also' answering the added καὶ before τοῖς μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ; the base ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ yields only 'gave to them'.
The added ὅτι is recitative before direct speech and leaves no trace in 'And he said unto them, The Son of man...'.
ASV 'The Son of man is lord of the sabbath' has no 'also'; the alternative's καὶ before τοῦ σαββάτου would be rendered 'lord also of the sabbath'.
ASV 'And it came to pass on another sabbath' renders no adverbial 'also' for the added καὶ, which versions following that reading print as 'And it came to pass also'.
Both orders give 'there was a man there'; English word order here is fixed by its own grammar.
Middle παρετηροῦντο and active παρετήρουν are alike 'watched' in ASV; no note bears on the voice.
'watched him' supplies an object English requires after 'watched'; translations of the shorter reading print 'him' as well, so the pronoun does not isolate αὐτὸν.
'whether he would heal on the sabbath' is the ordinary English of an indirect question after a past main verb, and fits present θεραπεύει as readily as future θεραπεύσει.
ASV 'that they might find how to accuse him' renders the infinitive κατηγορεῖν; the noun κατηγορίαν would give 'find an accusation against him'.
ASV 'and he said to the man' renders either εἶπεν δὲ or καὶ εἶπεν; ASV uses 'and' for both connectives.
ἀνδρὶ and ἀνθρώπῳ are both 'the man' in ASV here; nothing in the verse marks the distinction.
Ἔγειρε and Ἔγειραι are orthographic variants of the same imperative, rendered 'Rise up' either way.
'And he arose and stood forth' fits καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη and ὁ δὲ ἀναστὰς ἔστη alike; the subject pronoun is required by English regardless.
ASV opens 'And Jesus said unto them'; οὖν is rendered 'therefore'/'then' in ASV, and no such word appears.
ASV 'I ask you' is present tense, rendering Ἐπερωτῶ; the future Ἐπερωτήσω would give 'I will ask you'.
ASV puts a direct question, 'Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good, or to do harm?', rendering εἰ; τί ἔξεστιν would give 'what is lawful'.
Singular τῷ σαββάτῳ and plural τοῖς σάββασιν are both 'on the sabbath' in ASV usage.
ASV 'to save a life, or to destroy it' renders ἀπολέσαι; ἀποκτεῖναι would be 'to kill'.
ASV ends 'and his hand was restored', with neither 'as the other' nor 'whole as the other' following.
'that he went out into the mountain' renders the accusative-and-infinitive and the finite verb alike.
ASV writes 'and James and John' at this junction of the apostle list; the reading that omits καὶ leaves asyndeton, which ASV points with a comma.
ASV writes 'and Philip and Bartholomew'; the conjunction is rendered, as it is not where the list is asyndetic.
ASV continues 'and Matthew and Thomas', rendering the connective καὶ that the other reading drops.
ASV writes 'and James the son of Alphaeus', rendering the καὶ before Ἰάκωβον.
'James the son of Alphaeus' supplies 'the son of' for a bare genitive either way; the added τὸν τοῦ is invisible in English.
ASV writes 'and Judas the son of James', rendering the καὶ that the other reading omits.
Ἰσκαριὼθ and Ἰσκαριώτην are both transliterated 'Iscariot'.
ASV 'who became a traitor' has no 'also'; ὃς καὶ ἐγένετο would be rendered 'who also became'.
ASV 'a great multitude of his disciples' renders πολὺς with ὄχλος; the reading omitting it would leave 'a multitude'.
ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ and ὀχλούμενοι ὑπὸ are alike 'troubled with unclean spirits'.
ASV makes one clause, 'they that were troubled with unclean spirits were healed'; the added καὶ before ἐθεραπεύοντο gives the resumptive 'and they were healed', which ASV does not print.
English 'sought' is unmarked for number, so plural ἐζήτουν and singular ἐζήτει after πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος are indistinguishable.
ASV 'for in the same manner did their fathers' renders κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ; κατὰ ταῦτα would be 'according to these things'.
ASV 'ye that are full now' renders νῦν in the first woe; the reading omitting it gives only 'ye that are full'.
ASV's second woe reads 'Woe unto you, ye that laugh now', with the dative ὑμῖν rendered; the bare οὐαί would give 'Woe, ye that laugh now'.
'shall speak well of you' fixes its own English order; either Greek order yields it.
ASV 'when all men shall speak well of you' renders πάντες; the reading omitting it leaves 'when men shall speak well of you'.
ASV 'for in the same manner did their fathers' renders κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ, not ταῦτα.
'them that despitefully use you' does not show whether ἐπηρεαζόντων took the accusative or the dative.
περὶ and ὑπὲρ with προσεύχεσθε are both 'pray for'.

ASV begins 'Give to every one that asketh thee' with no connective, but sentence-initial δέ in a run of imperatives is regularly left untranslated, so its absence does not exclude the longer reading; the added article is invisible.
ASV 'do ye also to them likewise' renders an explicit καὶ ὑμεῖς; the base would give only 'do to them likewise'.
ASV opens the verse 'And if ye do good to them that do good to you' with no causal 'for'; the added γὰρ would give 'For if'.
ASV 'for even sinners do the same' renders both γὰρ ('for') and καὶ ('even'); the base καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ gives 'even sinners' alone, as ASV in fact prints at 6:34.
'And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive' fits all three spellings and moods; English 'if ye lend' does not distinguish subjunctive from indicative.
λαβεῖν and ἀπολαβεῖν are alike 'to receive' in 'of whom ye hope to receive'.
ASV 'even sinners lend to sinners' has 'even' for καὶ but no 'for'; the added γὰρ would give 'for even sinners', which ASV does print at 6:33.
ASV 'Be ye merciful' has no inferential particle; γίνεσθε οὖν would be 'Be ye therefore merciful'.
ASV renders καθώς as 'even as' by regular practice, so 'even as your Father is merciful' does not show whether καὶ stood after it.
ASV opens 'And judge not', rendering the initial καὶ that the other reading omits.
ASV lists 'pressed down, shaken together, running over' asyndetically; the reading with καὶ on either side of σεσαλευμένον would give 'and shaken together and running over'.
ASV 'For with what measure ye mete' renders ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ; the longer reading with αὐτῷ would give 'with the same measure that ye mete'.
ASV 'And he spake also a parable unto them' renders the adverbial καὶ as 'also'.
ἐμπεσοῦνται and πεσοῦνται with εἰς βόθυνον are both 'fall into a pit'.
'The disciple is not above his teacher' uses the possessive English idiom requires for a definite relational noun, so 'his' does not isolate an added αὐτοῦ.
ASV opens 'Or how canst thou say to thy brother', rendering the disjunctive ἢ before πῶς.
English fixes 'let me cast out the mote that is in thine eye' in verb-object order whatever the position of ἐκβαλεῖν in the Greek clause.
ASV 'nor again a corrupt tree that bringeth forth good fruit' renders πάλιν as 'again'.
'nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes' fits either Greek order; the English inversion follows from the fronted 'nor'.
ASV 'out of the good treasure of his heart' renders αὐτοῦ; the reading omitting it gives 'of the heart'.
'the evil man' supplies the noun English needs for a substantival adjective, so it does not show whether ἄνθρωπος stood in the Greek.

ASV's second clause reads 'out of the evil treasure' with no 'of his heart', though it prints that phrase in the first clause; the expansion θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας αὑτοῦ is therefore absent, and 'treasure' carries over from the parallel.
'out of the abundance of the heart' renders the phrase with or without its articles.
ASV reads 'because it had been well builded' and places the rival reading in a mapped textual_variant note, 'Many ancient authorities read for it had been founded upon the rock'.
ASV 'straightway it fell in' renders the compound συνέπεσεν; simple ἔπεσεν gives only 'it fell'.
